priceSnapshot.note: Midnight asked one question and the tape answered it cleanly. The 4H bar that opened at 04:00Z settled 63,833.3, which is 90.4 points ABOVE the 4H EMA200 at 63,742.93 - the reclaim survived its second consecutive settle, and midnight's 'coin balanced on its edge' fell to the upside. The bar that opened at 08:00Z then settled 64,236.3, an expansion of 403.0 points on the close and 490.9 points of clear air above the EMA200. That is no longer a reclaim being defended; it is a reclaim being extended. The 1H sequence of descending highs midnight logged - 63,923.2, 63,892.1, 63,873.0, 63,844.2, 63,800.0 - was broken on the 09:00Z bar, which printed 64,106.3 and closed 64,104.6, and the four bars since have made higher highs and higher closes in an unbroken chain: 64,106.3 / 64,221.3 / 64,248.1 / 64,254.0. The composition of the move is the encouraging part. Realized short liquidations have gone from $828,738 at the midnight read to $1,419,973 now, so $591,235 of shorts were flushed in 4.7 hours, while the long-side total moved $2,037 - effectively zero. This advance was paid for by trapped shorts, not by fresh long leverage. The long/short account ratio has eased 1.77 to 1.68, funding has fallen from +0.00702% to +0.00384% per 8h, and open interest is up only 0.79% to $2,062,574,395. A rally on falling long-crowding, near-zero funding and marginal open-interest growth is the healthiest version of this move available. Two things cap the conviction. The 15m RSI is 72.41, which is stretched on the fast chart into an event, and July CPI prints at 12:30Z - thirty minutes after this report is stamped. Consensus is +0.1% m/m and 3.4% headline with core at 2.5% versus 2.6% prior. Everything below is written for a market that has repaired its intermediate structure and is about to be handed a number that can undo it.

reduceIf.confirmation: TWO settled 1H closes below $63,700, or one close below plus a failure to reclaim on the very next bar. The line moves up 200 points from midnight's 63,500 because the structure it protects has moved: 63,700 sits underneath the 4H EMA200 at 63,742.93, which is the level this entire thesis rests on, and it is also the $1,067,270 realized-liquidation shelf. The confirmation stays deliberately wide for the reason this desk wrote into its own ledger two sessions ago - a reduce line sitting INSIDE a liquidation cluster measures a sweep, not a trend, and its base rate for reversing immediately is high. A CPI print at 12:30Z is exactly the kind of event that produces a single violent close through a shelf and then takes it straight back. The second close is the difference between selling the reaction and selling the break.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $64,300 on the 13:00Z bar or later - that is, AFTER the CPI print has been absorbed, not into it. 64,300 is chosen because it clears three things at once: the daily EMA20 at 64,255.95, which price has not closed above since 10 August; the session high of 64,254.0; and the 1H EMA100 at 64,285.27, the last hourly average still overhead. Above there the realized-liquidation ladder is close to empty - $92,731 at 64,400 and $203,040 at 64,500, $295,771 in total against $6,923,622 below - so a post-print close through 64,300 has very little friction in front of it up to the 64,650 area.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from HOLD to ADD, and it is the published rule firing rather than a change of mind. Endday wrote the add trigger as a settled 1H close above $63,930 WITH open interest FALLING across the same bar, and midnight carried it forward unchanged. Both halves were met on the 10:00Z bar: it closed 64,138.3, which is 208.3 points above the price line, and aggregate BTC open interest fell from $2,674,966,290 to $2,664,597,747 across that same hour, -0.39%. The 09:00Z bar met the price half but failed the open-interest half - OI rose 0.35% across it - which is precisely the discrimination the inversion was written to make, and it worked. Honouring a falsifiable trigger you set yourself, in advance, on the bar it fires, is the whole point of writing it down. What tempers the size is the other half of the inheritance: endday reserved the free cash for the CPI reaction and not the anticipation, and midnight reaffirmed it. Both were right. So this session deploys a partial tranche - roughly 30% of the free cash - and keeps the rest for the print. The resting stop moves up from 63,380 to 63,480, just beneath the $1,735,801 shelf at 63,500 that is still the largest single cluster on the 24-hour tape. It is not tightened further despite the 497-point advance, because ATR(14) on the 4H is 423.37 and a CPI whipsaw inside one ATR of spot would take out anything closer without saying anything about the trend.

liquidityMagnet.note: Measured, not estimated, and the headline asymmetry needs a caveat this session that it did not need before. Summed by side of spot, the shelves below now carry $6,923,622 and the shelves above carry $295,771, a ratio of 23.4x - but that number is mostly an artefact of the 497-point advance, which moved price above shelves that were overhead five hours ago. The honest reading is directional rather than absolute: above spot the realized-liquidation ladder is nearly empty, so an advance meets very little friction between here and 64,650; below spot the ladder is dense but the mass sits 500 to 1,000 points away and only becomes a magnet again if 63,900 gives way. That is why pull is marked balanced rather than down. The long/short split of the same tape is the more informative number and it has genuinely improved: $5,799,420 of longs against $1,419,973 of shorts over 24 hours, a 4.08x ratio, down from 7.0x at midnight. Shorts absorbed $591,235 of that in the last 4.7 hours while the long total moved $2,037. Standard caveat - this is REALIZED liquidation data, a map of where leverage has already been flushed, not a forward book of resting orders.

scalpContext.intradayBias: A 612.7-point range since the midnight mark, 63,641.3 to 64,254.0, and price is sitting at the very top of it, 20.2 points off the high. The structure is a clean five-bar advance with no pullback worth the name - the deepest retrace on the 1H was 44.8 points. That is a trend, and trends into an event print are the worst thing to fade and the worst thing to chase. The 15m RSI at 72.41 says the immediate edge is gone. The realistic scalp map is a break of 64,300 after the print, or a rejection back under 64,000 that hands the initiative back to the shelf at 63,900.

calibration.note: Midnight's reduce at 63,500 was never approached - the lowest 1H close in the window was 63,797.7 on the 08:00Z bar and the lowest wick was 63,641.3 - so priorReduceFired is false. The add trigger DID fire, and it fired on exactly the discrimination it was designed to make. Endday wrote it as a settled 1H close above 63,930 WITH open interest FALLING across the same bar, and inverted the open-interest condition on purpose so that a retail chase into a crowded long book would not qualify. The 09:00Z bar closed 64,104.6, clearing the price line by 174.6 points, but aggregate BTC open interest ROSE 0.35% across it, so it did not qualify. The 10:00Z bar closed 64,138.3 and open interest FELL 0.39%, from $2,674,966,290 to $2,664,597,747, so it did. One bar of patience, produced by a condition written five hours earlier, and the entry it gave was 33.7 points better than the one it declined. actingHelped is marked true: midnight's HOLD carried 0.00232786 BTC of spot through a 497.1-point advance, worth about +$1.16 unrealized, and it correctly refused to trim into a level 236.7 points away. The honest qualification is that HOLD also left 48.89 USDT idle through the whole move, so the decision was right on the position it had and cost opportunity on the cash it did not deploy - which is precisely the trade-off the reserved-for-CPI reasoning accepted in advance. This is the first session in four where a correct process produced a positive outcome.
